title: How Science Changes Its Mind
objective: After this level you can explain how new evidence overturned accepted ideas, such as bacteria causing most stomach ulcers.
summary: In 1982 ulcers were blamed on stress and lifestyle. Warren and Marshall found a bacterium, Marshall infected himself, and cures that killed the bacteria settled it: a Nobel Prize in 2005.

cards.headline: In 1984 a doctor infected himself on purpose.
cards.body: Barry Marshall's results were widely disbelieved, so he made himself the test subject. His story shows how science changes its mind: slowly, then for good.

cards.headline: What everyone knew
cards.body: In 1982, stress and lifestyle were considered the major causes of peptic ulcers. Then pathologist Robin Warren noticed curved bacteria in stomach samples, always near inflammation. Marshall grew the unknown bacterium in the lab, and together they found it in almost all patients with stomach inflammation or ulcers. The accepted idea had a rival.

cards.headline: Evidence that wouldn't go away
cards.body: Marshall infected himself with the bacteria and developed stomach inflammation. Treatment studies did the rest. Ulcers healed by cutting stomach acid kept coming back, but patients were cured once the bacteria were wiped out. Today a short course of antibiotics and acid inhibitors can cure an ulcer.

cards.headline: How the mind changed
cards.body: Helicobacter pylori is now firmly established as the cause of most ulcers: more than 90% of duodenal ulcers and up to 80% of gastric ones. In 2005 Marshall and Warren won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. The switch took years, and that's normal: changing an accepted theory is a community process, and good ideas aren't always recognized right away. What finally tipped it was the evidence.

cards.headline: Changing minds: explained
learned: In 1982, ulcers were blamed on stress and lifestyle
Warren and Marshall found a bacterium in ulcer patients
Cures that killed the bacteria settled the case
Accepted theories change, slowly, with evidence

questions.prompt: In 1982, what were considered the major causes of peptic ulcers?

options.label: A stomach bacterium
options.rationale: That was the new idea, not the accepted one.

options.label: Inherited genes alone
options.rationale: The accepted view blamed stress and lifestyle.

options.label: Viruses caught in childhood
options.rationale: The accepted view blamed stress and lifestyle.

questions.explanation: When Marshall and Warren found the bacterium in 1982, stress and lifestyle were considered the major causes.

questions.prompt: Why did treatment studies help persuade doctors that bacteria cause ulcers?

options.label: Cutting stomach acid cured ulcers for good
Patients preferred antibiotics to other drugs
options.rationale: Preference is not evidence of cause.

options.label: A famous journal said so first
Patients stayed cured once the bacteria were wiped out

questions.explanation: Acid-cutting treatment let ulcers return; killing the bacteria cured them, which points to the bacteria as the cause.

questions.prompt: The old view that stress and lifestyle cause ulcers turned out wrong. In Level 4's terms, what was it?

options.label: A factual claim, just a mistaken one
A matter of personal taste
options.rationale: It could be checked by research, as it was.

options.label: A value judgment
options.rationale: It says what causes ulcers, not what ought to be.

options.label: Not a claim at all
options.rationale: It was true or false, so it was a claim.

questions.explanation: It could be checked by observation and research. Being wrong made it an erroneous factual claim, not a different kind of statement.
